summary: St. Joe National Forest lookout: camp c.1924, 14x14 ft log cabin 1930, destroyed 1953; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1953 according to all three sources

events.note: Destroyed; the sources give no cause

evidence.supports: Camp in 1924, 14x14 log cabin in 1930, patrol two miles south atop Crooked Ridge, destroyed 1953
evidence.quote: 1924: camp. 1930: 14x14' log cab. Patrol 2 miles south atop Crooked Ridge. Destroyed 1953.

evidence.supports: Location about eight miles northeast of Red Ives Ranger Station
evidence.quote: 8 miles northeast of Red Ives R.S.

evidence.supports: Listed in Shoshone County, Idaho and Mineral County, Montana
Agency given as St. Joe/Lolo National Forests
Patrol point two miles south atop Crooked Ridge
evidence.quote: Patrol point 2 miles south atop Crooked Ridge

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Fire Lookout gives St. Joe/Lolo National Forests; Idaho Fire Lookouts and Forest Lookouts give only the St. Joe National Forest. The story uses St. Joe National Forest.

notes_for_editor: The three sites agree on the 1924 camp, the 1930 cabin and the 1953 destruction, but none is a primary record and none gives a cause. Idaho Fire Lookouts tags the site Drive-Up; that may describe the historic approach, and no source says whether a road reaches the site now, so no access level is recorded. The brief's county field reads Shoshone/ Mineral (MT); the sources list both. The Weebly page has a staff name only on Idaho Fire Lookouts. Elevation 7,052 ft is recorded in the story only.
